questions.def: Cleft sentences use 'that' to emphasize the identified element.
questions.question: It was the rain ___ caused the flooding.

questions.def: This 'what' cleft focuses on the need for patience.
questions.question: It ___ I need is a little patience.

questions.def: 'Were' needs to agree with 'students' (plural), so 'was'.
questions.question: It were the students who organized the protest.

questions.def: It + verb needs to agree in number and tense.
questions.question: It ___ the importance of careful planning.

questions.def: 'What' clefts often use 'for' before the object.
questions.question: What I want is ___ you to be happy.

questions.def: Use 'then that' to emphasize the point of realization.
questions.question: It was only ___ I realized my mistake.

questions.def: A simple 'is' creates a basic cleft sentence.
questions.question: It ___ her dedication to the project.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the element that is being emphasized.
questions.question: ___ I need is a good night's sleep.

questions.def: 'What' refers to the thing he was waiting for.
questions.question: It was ___ he had been waiting for.

questions.def: 'What I expect' correctly completes the cleft sentence.
questions.question: It ___ a difficult task.

questions.def: 'Through' emphasizes the means by which success was achieved.
questions.question: It was ___ his help that we succeeded.

questions.def: 'Is not' provides the correct negative cleft construction.
questions.question: It ___ that I feel uncomfortable.

questions.def: 'Is what' correctly introduces the emphasized element.
questions.question: It ___ most is their safety.

questions.def: 'The' specifies a particular principle.
questions.question: It wasn't the money, but ___ principle, that mattered.

questions.def: 'It is this' correctly introduces the topic of discussion.
questions.question: ___ that I want to discuss today.

questions.def: Correct cleft construction emphasizing the person blamed.
questions.question: It ___ for the error.

questions.def: 'That' is commonly used after 'all' in cleft constructions.
questions.question: All ___ I want is a quiet life.

questions.def: A noun phrase is needed to specify 'what' made the difference.
questions.question: It was ___ that made the difference.

questions.def: This complete construction emphasizes honesty.
questions.question: It ___ most is honesty.

questions.def: 'Their' indicates possession, whose decision it was.
questions.question: It was ___ decision to leave early.

questions.def: 'Was thanks to' correctly indicates the cause of something.
questions.question: It ___ the support of the community.

questions.def: Correct negative cleft for the element not of importance.
questions.question: It ___ is the principle.

questions.def: 'Consistent' modifies 'hard work', describing the type of work.
questions.question: It is ___ hard work that pays off.

questions.def: 'It is precisely this' emphasizes the point of disagreement.
questions.question: ___ that I disagree with.

questions.def: 'That' introduces the clause specifying what impressed him.
questions.question: It was the novel ___ impressed him most.

questions.def: 'What' introduces a noun clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ surprised everyone was her sudden resignation.

questions.def: The verb must agree with the singular subject 'it': 'was'.
questions.question: It were his dedication and perseverance that led to success.

questions.def: Cleft sentence correctly emphasizes 'quality' using 'that' clause.
questions.question: It ___ quality over quantity.

questions.def: A cleft sentence needs a noun phrase after 'was'.
questions.question: It was ___ she found most challenging.

questions.def: 'What' introduces the noun clause acting as the subject.
questions.question: ___ she needs is more time to dedicate to research.
